metas.name: A Type Car
metas.note:
Car meta is, for better or worse, a powerful way to narrow down your guesses in Kazakhstan. In this map, you will first learn to distinguish the basic types of car. You can get used to doing a quick check on every round: Season, car, driving direction. Once you are familiar with these identifications, the second map in the series will go into detail on how to best use that info.

A Type has a slender black rubber antenna. You can tell that a wire spirals around it under the rubber one or two times. It is also called the "screw antenna". In the left forward corner of the truck bed, there is a metal bracket mounted directly to the side of the truck. It can hold a wire, but the wire doesn't change the type of car.
metas.footer: Based on docs by DeSlagen, @nem.__., Plonkit, @kotyu and @rhaubain_brbs, @Capi, Yoav, griffithdidnothingwrong. Thanks to ra1n & nem for consulting.

metas.name: Aktau vibes
metas.note: Light yellow brick. Sand. The sea to the West and a bit of elevation. Gold-rimmed white street signs with Cyrillic and Latin text. Summer coverage, bright skies. Aktau!
metas.footer: Based on docs by DeSlagen, @nem.__., Plonkit, @kotyu and @rhaubain_brbs, @Capi, Yoav, griffithdidnothingwrong. Thanks to ra1n & nem for consulting.

metas.name: Almaty vibes
metas.note: Footage in Almaty was taken in November and in the spring, so the city looks distinctly and uniquely wintery, with the occasional fresh grass coming up.
metas.footer: Based on docs by DeSlagen, @nem.__., Plonkit, @kotyu and @rhaubain_brbs, @Capi, Yoav, griffithdidnothingwrong. Thanks to ra1n & nem for consulting.

metas.name: Astana vibes
metas.note: Astana used to be called Nur-Sultan. A lot of signs still say that. It's a very large city with very large buildings, wide boulevards, and a comparatively affluent vibe, and care has been taken to make it presentable and look nice. The footage was taken in Summer, and the city is looking its best.
metas.footer: Based on docs by DeSlagen, @nem.__., Plonkit, @kotyu and @rhaubain_brbs, @Capi, Yoav, griffithdidnothingwrong. Thanks to ra1n & nem for consulting.

metas.name: Big Mountains
metas.note: The Southeast of the country is the only place with anything taller than a hill visible. The mountains reach impressive heights and the largest ridges are snowcapped.
metas.footer: Based on docs by DeSlagen, @nem.__., Plonkit, @kotyu and @rhaubain_brbs, @Capi, Yoav, griffithdidnothingwrong. Thanks to ra1n & nem for consulting.

metas.name: Birches and fields
metas.note: In the central northern part of the country, Big green fields are punctuated by copses of birches, lush and green. The roads are also often lined with rows of other trees and tall, healthy shrubs.
metas.footer: Based on docs by DeSlagen, @nem.__., Plonkit, @kotyu and @rhaubain_brbs, @Capi, Yoav, griffithdidnothingwrong. Thanks to ra1n & nem for consulting.

metas.name: C Type Car
metas.note:
Car meta is, for better or worse, a powerful way to narrow down your guesses in Kazakhstan. In this map, you will first learn to distinguish the basic types of car. You can get used to doing a quick check on every round: Season, car, driving direction. Once you are familiar with these identifications, the second map in the series will go into detail on how to best use that info.

C Type has an antenna with a stubby look, with many tiny ridges. It is also called the "rattlesnake antenna". This car can have a bracket, a wire in the truck bed, or a support bar across the back edge of the cabin. All of these combinations count as C Type.
metas.footer: Based on docs by DeSlagen, @nem.__., Plonkit, @kotyu and @rhaubain_brbs, @Capi, Yoav, griffithdidnothingwrong. Thanks to ra1n & nem for consulting.

metas.name: D Type Car
metas.note:
Car meta is, for better or worse, a powerful way to narrow down your guesses in Kazakhstan. In this map, you will first learn to distinguish the basic types of car. You can get used to doing a quick check on every round: Season, car type, wire, driving direction. Once you are familiar with these identifications, the second map in the series will go into detail on how to best use that info.

D Type actually has the same antenna type as C Type, but it is folded backward to point directly at the camera. This car can have a bracket, a wire in the truck bed, or a support bar across the back edge of the cabin. All of these combinations count as D Type.

metas.name: Desert and Shrubs
metas.note: Sandy soil, very arid landscapes and small, dry-looking bushes dominate the Southwest of the country.
metas.footer: Based on docs by DeSlagen, @nem.__., Plonkit, @kotyu and @rhaubain_brbs, @Capi, Yoav, griffithdidnothingwrong. Thanks to ra1n & nem for consulting.

metas.name: Fall
metas.note:
Google started covering Kazakhstan in August 22 in the capital, Astana, and basically went around the country clockwise over the next year. The changing seasons over that year are a great clue for where in the country you are.

During the fall, Google covered the Northeast. It can be tricky to tell late summer and early fall apart, but generally, things start looking just a little more wilted and less lush and, for lack of a better word, juicy, Once fall is in full swing, there is seldom any doubt about the season: lots of deciduous trees show off their colors, and things start to look more and more orange.
metas.footer: Based on docs by DeSlagen, @nem.__., Plonkit, @kotyu and @rhaubain_brbs, @Capi, Yoav, griffithdidnothingwrong. Thanks to ra1n & nem for consulting.

metas.name: Fall hills
metas.note: In the East Kazakhstan Region, north of Oskemen, footage was taken of sometimes quite substantial hills during fall. If you see red leaves and hills, this is where you should guess.
metas.footer: Based on docs by DeSlagen, @nem.__., Plonkit, @kotyu and @rhaubain_brbs, @Capi, Yoav, griffithdidnothingwrong. Thanks to ra1n & nem for consulting.

metas.name: Golden hills
metas.note: In the central southern part of the country, by the Usbek border near Shymkent, you will find rolling hills with golden grass. Further east, you will start to see big mountains in the distance and the hills will be more green. Further south, the landscape becomes drier, flatter again, and then more agricultural.
metas.footer: Based on docs by DeSlagen, @nem.__., Plonkit, @kotyu and @rhaubain_brbs, @Capi, Yoav, griffithdidnothingwrong. Thanks to ra1n & nem for consulting.

metas.name: Green hills
metas.note: Between Shymkent and Almaty, but especially northeast of Bishkek, you will find hills with green grass on them, sometimes with bigger mountains visible in the distance. The hills range from the wide and rolling to an almost Scottish-looking landscape.
metas.footer: Based on docs by DeSlagen, @nem.__., Plonkit, @kotyu and @rhaubain_brbs, @Capi, Yoav, griffithdidnothingwrong. Thanks to ra1n & nem for consulting.

metas.name: Green plains
metas.note: All over the Northwest, vast, flat open plains with green grass can be found. Occasional groups of trees and bushes can dot the landscape or line the road for a little stretch, especially around civilization. Around Aktobe, in the West, the landscape can become a tiny bit less flat.
metas.footer: Based on docs by DeSlagen, @nem.__., Plonkit, @kotyu and @rhaubain_brbs, @Capi, Yoav, griffithdidnothingwrong. Thanks to ra1n & nem for consulting.

metas.name: No Antenna/Blurred Car
metas.note:
Car meta is, for better or worse, a powerful way to narrow down your guesses in Kazakhstan. In this map, you will first learn to distinguish the basic types of car. You can get used to doing a quick check on every round: Season, car, driving direction. Once you are familiar with these identifications, the second map in the series will go into detail on how to best use that info.

Throughout the whole country, and independently of the car type, the antenna can have been removed using image processing, or the car been blurred. In some cases, you will still be able to tell which antenna type it is by the reflection in the car's roof or other features of the car (for instance, if you see a support bar or no bracket, it cannot be Type A or B), but sometimes not. "No antenna" is not its own type of car, just obscured information. "Blurred car" likewise is not its own category, but it can be useful for identifying a small number of places that get it very consistently for longer stretches.
metas.footer: Based on docs by DeSlagen, @nem.__., Plonkit, @kotyu and @rhaubain_brbs, @Capi, Yoav, griffithdidnothingwrong. Thanks to ra1n & nem for consulting.

metas.name: Oskemen vibes
metas.note: Oskemen was covered in October, so the leaves are perhaps a little further along in their color change than in the otherwise similar-looking Pavlodar and Semey. Another way to tell the three apart are the buses: Oskemen uses a variety of buses in different colors, while the ones in Pavlodar are all green and those in Semey are all green with a white bottom. In any event, fall coverage in a big city should only be in Pavlodar, Semey or Oskemen.
metas.footer: Based on docs by DeSlagen, @nem.__., Plonkit, @kotyu and @rhaubain_brbs, @Capi, Yoav, griffithdidnothingwrong. Thanks to ra1n & nem for consulting.

metas.name: Pavlodar vibes
metas.note: Pavlodar was covered in September, so the leaves are in the process of turning orange, but it doesn't feel too cold yet. It's kind of pleasant and sunny, which can be an indicator to tell it apart from the otherwise similar-looking Semey. In any event, fall coverage in a big city should only be in Pavlodar, Semey or Oskemen.
metas.footer: Based on docs by DeSlagen, @nem.__., Plonkit, @kotyu and @rhaubain_brbs, @Capi, Yoav, griffithdidnothingwrong. Thanks to ra1n & nem for consulting.

metas.name: Ridder vibes
metas.note: The twin towns of Ridder and Leninogorsk are situated in a flat valley, surrounded by substantial mountains which are visible from almost everywhere. There are a lot of wooden houses on the outskirts, and the area looks fairly dreary. The inner city does have bigger apartment blocks. The footage was taken in fall, with orange leaves.
metas.footer: Based on docs by DeSlagen, @nem.__., Plonkit, @kotyu and @rhaubain_brbs, @Capi, Yoav, griffithdidnothingwrong. Thanks to ra1n & nem for consulting.

metas.name: Semey vibes
metas.note: Semey was covered in September, with leaves just starting to turn orange. You will find a lot of brick facades with contrasty mortar, and many houses feature blue elements. Dark wooden houses are also common. The city uses a unique livery on their buses, green with a white bottom. The footage looks perhaps a little less sunny than the otherwise similar Pavlodar. In any event, fall coverage in a big city should only be in Pavlodar, Semey or Oskemen.
metas.footer: Based on docs by DeSlagen, @nem.__., Plonkit, @kotyu and @rhaubain_brbs, @Capi, Yoav, griffithdidnothingwrong. Thanks to ra1n & nem for consulting.

metas.name: Shymkent vibes
metas.note: Freshly sprouted lush bright green leaves and grass characterize the April footage in Shymkent. There is a certain grayness to the atmosphere. (Frustratingly, some summer coverage exists in the city, too.) The city center features wide boulevards with trees planted between lanes. The architecture of the suburbs has mostly low wide slanted roofs, while garages frequently have rounded roofs. Colorful houses are relatively common, some of the neighbourhoods are even color-coordinated. Shymkent is one of just three cities that have prominent yellow electricity boxes.
metas.footer: Based on docs by DeSlagen, @nem.__., Plonkit, @kotyu and @rhaubain_brbs, @Capi, Yoav, griffithdidnothingwrong. Thanks to ra1n & nem for consulting.

metas.name: Snow coverage
metas.note: There will be snow on the ground, sometimes a fully white field and sometimes just a few almost-molten remains, around, in, and east of Almaty, in the Southeast.
metas.footer: Based on docs by DeSlagen, @nem.__., Plonkit, @kotyu and @rhaubain_brbs, @Capi, Yoav, griffithdidnothingwrong. Thanks to ra1n & nem for consulting.

metas.name: Summer
metas.note:
Google started covering Kazakhstan in August 22 in the capital, Astana, and basically went around the country clockwise over the next year. The changing seasons over that year are a great clue for where in the country you are.

The whole western half was covered in June and July, bigger plants (where available) are in full deep green foliage and there's a palpable sense of heat in many areas. In the more deserty areas, things look deserty, but even there you get green tufts of grass sometimes. The grass turns yellow a little earlier than the trees, so it can be tricky to discern it from fall coverage sometimes, especially in August footage in the central and northern part of Kazakhstan.
metas.footer: Based on docs by DeSlagen, @nem.__., Plonkit, @kotyu and @rhaubain_brbs, @Capi, Yoav, griffithdidnothingwrong. Thanks to ra1n & nem for consulting.

metas.name: Wavy steppe
metas.note: In a large area around Karaganda, the landscape is mostly an empty steppe with very slight hills, if you can even call most of them that. It's just not completely flat, but sort of wavy. You get bits of vegetation other than grass in some parts, but not a whole lot. Most of this area was covered in late summer and early fall, so the grass is changing color. The big exception is the road south out of Karaganda, which was covered in November and is noticeably more wintery.
metas.footer: Based on docs by DeSlagen, @nem.__., Plonkit, @kotyu and @rhaubain_brbs, @Capi, Yoav, griffithdidnothingwrong. Thanks to ra1n & nem for consulting.

metas.name: Winter & Spring
metas.note:
Google started covering Kazakhstan in August 22 in the capital, Astana, and basically went around the country clockwise over the next year. The changing seasons over that year are a great clue for where in the country you are.

The winter coverage starts in November, leaving Karaganda south toward Almaty. The grass is brown and dead-looking, the trees are barren. Coverage then continues in early spring (March and eventually April), exploring the Southeast of the country and ending up back where the journey started, in Turkistan. Trees will sometimes still be barren, or producing the first buds and even bright green leaves. The grass is springing up lush and green in parts already. Much of this season is still covered in snow.
metas.footer: Based on docs by DeSlagen, @nem.__., Plonkit, @kotyu and @rhaubain_brbs, @Capi, Yoav, griffithdidnothingwrong. Thanks to ra1n & nem for consulting.
